#### What this PR does / why we need it:

> if there's not a kubelet approver with context who can say whether this should apply to static pods or not, are we confident leaving this in for 1.27?

That's the question, innit?    @derekwaynecarr @mrunalp @SergeyKanzhelev @bobbypage - this whole feature is at risk of rollback.  Help?

I think we could get away with saying that static pods are explicitly not supported for now, but I'm not sure that solves the problem.  Are we OK with a gate which can disrupt more than its own feature?  It seems fair game to me, but not ideal, obv.

We discussed this today in SIG-Node meeting. The consensus in meeting is that VPA should not apply to static pods because the source of truth for static pods is the manifest stored on the disk. (xref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/116262#issuecomment-1468558194). There are two cases to consider:

1) stand-alone kubelet: In this case, the kubelet is running in standalone and not connected to the API server. VPA doesn't make sense as there is no API-sever to initiate resize
2) static pods with kubelet connected to api server. In this case, a mirror pod is created to represent the pod manifest stored on disk, but the mirror pod is intended to be "read only" and not controlled via the api. 

So in both cases, it makes sense to ignore static pods for VPA.

> if there's not a kubelet approver with context who can say whether this should apply to static pods or not, are we confident leaving this in for 1.27?

We discussed at today's SIG Node, and here is what I preferred and SIG Node community agreed:

1) The source of the true for the static pods are those manifest files. I don't think VPA feature should apply to the static pods at the first place.
2) Non-standalone Kubelet mode, those static pods will have a corresponding mirror pods created. In this case, the scheduler can take the static pods / mirror pods into the consideration at the admission time. 
3) In standalone kubelet case, there is no mirror pods created; hence the pod admission will be only evaluated at node level as the last defense. 

With all 3 reasons, we think VPA should exclude the static pods. The intention of PR is correct. 

But I haven't figure out the root cause of the initial null point issue yet since none of us reproduce the issue.

Sorry, I wish I'd known that was a question, I could definitely have said this does *not* apply to static pods because mirror pods are read-only sources of spec today (as david captured from sig-node).  Agree with the current summary for static pods.

In general though every place in the kubelet we have checked for static pods has later revealed a serious bug in our logic or a gap in our structure.  It's just that static pods *can* be resized via update, and they *can't* be resized via the API, and static pods *must* work without status writes propagating to an apiserver (i.e. pass into status manager and then back into podManager) for standalone.  That's another bug to go on my list - assuming that statusManager writes to the API server means any logic in the kubelet that relies on it breaks, and we shouldn't have to know that deep in the code (whether we're standalone) which means the logic for inplace needs to *not* have to have static pod checks in beta.

Captured this problem in https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1wbPFANXVbk-e-5BvVHaZScqoqJsfcU_FQVmG-N7pv3c/edit#slide=id.g1de9fa9d3b9_0_0

I've pretty much accepted that we'll need to devote significant time in 1.28 to finish correct state propagation, and inplace will help us do that.
The question is - who will take ownership for this PR review or make the call to back it out and try again next time?

No matter what in 1.28 I and others have to burn through problems 5-9 in the slide deck I created (inplace exposed 8, i think this new one is 10).  If we delay, we'll have more time to work through it, but we won't get early feedback, but we'll also derisk any other improvements that have to get done once master opens.

issue_context.title: VPA panics in standalone kubelets
issue_context.body:
1. Start a standalone kubelet (not registered to an API server)

2. Manager construction short-circuits `Start()` here:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/253ab3eda71f250ad6692bb16f035cebaf0651c9/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L186-L192

3. VPA state is never initialized here:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/253ab3eda71f250ad6692bb16f035cebaf0651c9/pkg/kubelet/status/status_manager.go#L195-L200

4. All pod syncs then panic on this line:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a1b12e49eac237a37939642d0c3395008b9ab380/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2412

```
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x18 pc=0x3b5f21f]

  pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go:2412 +0x4df
```

If you mean, when VPA points at a mirror pod can it change spec?  No, generally.  If you mean, should static pod consumed resources be visible via the API?  Yes.

> If you mean, when VPA points at a mirror pod can it change spec? No, generally.

From what we can tell, *something* in the VPA path (`computePodResizeAction `) thought a static pod's resources needed to trigger the resize code path.

I don't know enough about static pod handling to know if that is a category error and VPA should *never* expect to resize resources used by static pods. That's what part of the proposed fix in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/116504 does - excludes static pods from being considered by VPA.

For a kubelet running against an API server, would you expect manifest-driven pods to be able to make use of resize functionality? If so, a blanket exclusion of static pods from that code path doesn't seem correct.

> > . @smarterclayton, would you expect an updated manifest that changes resources to be handled by VPA?
> 
> If you mean, when VPA points at a mirror pod can it change spec? No, generally. If you mean, should static pod consumed resources be visible via the API? Yes.

I think the implementation can support resizing static pods via patch to its mirror. There is some bug in the pod update -> pod worker sync handoff where the resize update is lost. IMHO, we should allow resizing static pods as well via its mirror. (Standalone kubelet is a different story - the current implementation terminates and adds new pod). We just haven't considered this scenario and it needs a bit of work (mainly to develop solid e2e test cases for mirror pod resize and standalone scenario). This is something I'd want to take the time to fix the right way in 1.28, so my preference is to make a defensive fix for v1.27 (aka we don't support static pod resizing for 1.27 alpha) rather than trying to wing it.

In HandlePodUpdates, static pods are processed by handleMirrorPod:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fcf5d23e6818ccfbc92f332af82f31661f8d4f88/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2491-L2502
which dispatches SyncPodUpdate for the original pod, and not the updated mirror pod.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/fcf5d23e6818ccfbc92f332af82f31661f8d4f88/pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go#L2412-L2420

For normal pods, SyncPodUpdate is invoked for the updated pods. This is the reason (bug) I didn't see resize updates come through in SyncPod().

I don't know how long the code has been this way, but I'm hesitant and risk-averse to just swap out `pod` with `mirrorPod` so close to code freeze. This is why I feel it is best to disable static pods for resize at this time and do it right in 1.28
